LITE should be tracked as an EML/laser and datacom transceiver candidate; next validation should focus on whether EML or laser capacity is truly scarce versus merely high demand.
FN should be tracked as a second-order optical manufacturing capacity candidate rather than an optical IP owner; evidence needs customer/product-level AI exposure.
CRDO should be tracked as a high-speed copper/optical connectivity and AEC/DSP/retimer candidate for AI cluster fabrics.
CLS should be tracked as a 1.6TbE AI switch-platform and integration supplier tied to Broadcom Tomahawk 6 adoption.

Next Layer 1B pass should separately evaluate US-listed test/measurement and inspection suppliers for 800G/1.6T optics, including VIAV and Keysight, plus silicon photonics foundry/platform candidates such as GFS and Tower Semiconductor.
This pass did not include non-US primary listings such as Innolight and Eoptolink despite strong node relevance; they should be captured in a non-US or ADR/global-listings pass.

node: AI data-center networking, switching, optics, and interconnect
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the AI networking and optical-interconnect node toward direct scarce suppliers in 800G/1.6T optics, InP/EML photonic components, optical manufacturing, active electrical cables, retimers/DSPs, and 1.6TbE switching systems. This pass excludes already-obvious seed leaders such as Broadcom, Arista, NVIDIA, Marvell, Cisco, Amphenol, TE Connectivity, and Corning unless they appear as ecosystem dependencies. The strongest incremental candidates are Coherent, Lumentum, Fabrinet, Credo, and Celestica; all screen above USD 1B market cap based on cached finance data from June 5-6, 2026, but this is not a valuation opinion.
